_comment: Shipped defaults for the YourPHR TypeScript stack (yourphr#621). READ-ONLY: this file is the product, not the instance. An operator overrides values in <data dir>/config/app-custom-config.json, which holds ONLY what they changed — never a copy of this file. Keys prefixed with _ are comments and are ignored on load.
_comment_storage: yourphr#630 — YOURPHR_FAST_STORAGE and YOURPHR_SLOW_STORAGE are plain environment variables, not configuration keys: they are what LOCATE this file, so they cannot be set inside it. Both default to ./data, so a single-volume instance sets nothing. Fast holds small, hot, lock-dependent stores (the databases, config, .env); slow holds bulk and archives and is fine on a NAS. Every path below composes from one of them, so what goes where is decided HERE and not in code. SQLite must stay on the fast root — its locking is unsafe over NFS/SMB (yourphr#628).
_comment_environment_name: What this instance calls itself in the UI's version string — Go's web.environment_name. Published on /api/version as environment_name, and the ONLY source the footer has: the Angular bundle carries no name of its own, because one image serves every instance, so a name compiled in can only be a guess — and on yourphr#673 that guess told a production instance it was a sandbox. Set it either way: YOURPHR_WEB_ENVIRONMENT_NAME in <FAST_STORAGE>/.env, which is how a bare-metal operator running several daemons tells which one answered, or Admin -> Configuration when no variable is set. Deliberately NOT in yourphr.config.env-keys: declared ownership would make the variable the only source and the screen read-only forever, and this key wants both doors. 'demo' on demo.yourphr.org, which is how a visitor tells the two apart; 'yourPHR' is what an instance that has not renamed itself shows.
_comment_relay: yourphr#700 — the SMART OAuth store-and-poll relay (relay/README.md). public-url is what providers redirect the patient's browser to; <public-url>/callback is the redirect_uri registered with each FHIR vendor. url is where THIS instance polls /pending (defaults to public-url; may be private or cluster-internal — an operator-set relay is polled through a capability bound to that one origin, not the SSRF-guarded client, yourphr#749). secret gates /pending and is env-owned (YOURPHR_RELAY_SECRET) — set the same value on the app and the relay. With no URL set, the project dev/demo relay is used and the admin card says so.
_comment_signup_enabled: Self-service signup (yourphr#691). DEFAULT FALSE, deliberately: a self-hosted PHR reachable from the internet with an open signup form hands an account to whoever arrives first, and the first start already creates a bootstrap admin whose password is written to <data>/.admin_bootstrap_password — so nobody needs signup to get in. An operator who wants household members to register themselves turns it on; otherwise accounts are created at Admin -> Users. ngdpbase calls this ngdpbase.application.registration and splits it into a master policy plus a per-mechanism toggle for magic-link and OIDC; this stack has one mechanism (password), so it is one key. The name follows the WIRE format the Angular sign-in page already reads from /api/instance/public (signup.enabled) rather than ngdpbase's key name.
_comment_agent_token: Agent tokens (yourphr#695) — a credential a patient mints for THEMSELVES and hands to an agent (an AI client, a script) so it can read their records on their behalf. Adopted from ngdpbase's AgentTokenManager (its #946), after its #1108 review: opaque rather than JWT because a 24-hour credential must be revocable before it expires and a self-signed JWT cannot be withdrawn; SHA-256 rather than bcrypt because 256 bits of uniform randomness has no dictionary to attack, so a work factor only adds latency on an endpoint agents hammer. DEFAULT FALSE: this opens a second way into a PHI store, so an operator turns it on deliberately. SCOPES ARE ACCESS-LOG CATEGORIES ('Medications', 'Conditions', ...) rather than permission names, because the user role holds no permissions in this stack — a person reaches their own records by compartment, not by grant — so there was nothing for a scope to narrow. Binding scope to the log category means a surface that cannot be logged cannot be scoped, and makes the first cut read-only structurally rather than by a flag.
_comment_agent_token_read_only: First cut, and the setting that makes the rest safe to ship: no write scope exists, because only listed GET routes have an access category to name. Kept as an explicit key rather than left implicit so that adding a write surface later is a deliberate decision against a switch that is already off, not a silent widening.
_comment_agent_token_ttl: Hours. max-ttl-hours is the CEILING, not just the default — there is deliberately no 'never expires' option: the Go token this replaces had one, and expiration 0 resolved to 31 December 2099, which is how a permanent credential nobody remembers issuing comes to exist. Raising the ceiling is the temptation ('my agent should not re-authenticate daily') and the answer to that is a different mechanism with its own review, not a bigger number here.
_comment_agent_token_retention: Days a dead record (revoked or expired) is kept before it is dropped, so the account page can still show what was rotated and when. ZERO IS LEGAL and means what it says: drop a dead record as soon as it is dead. So is max-per-user 0, which means no token may be minted at all (yourphr#698 item 2 — a count and a retention window have a meaningful zero; a TTL and an interval do not, and a non-numeric value there falls back with a warning naming the key). The access log is unaffected — it is the Audit manager's, it outlives the token, and since yourphr#698 it is also where a mint, a renewal and a revocation are recorded, so the answer to 'what could this credential do, and when was it stopped?' survives the retention that takes the row.
_comment_agent_token_renewal: Renewal rotates a live token forward: a NEW secret, the same name and scopes, the old record revoked. Never a moved expiry date — a leaked secret then dies at its original expiry however many times the owner renews. It requires the OWNER'S SESSION: an agent token cannot renew itself or any other, because a delegation that can extend its own life is not delegated any more and a cap the token can lift is a cap on paper. renew-window-hours matters more than it looks: without it, 'renew' is a button pressed on day one and the life is unbounded from the start. max-renewals 0 means unlimited; a number forces a fresh mint and re-consent after N rotations.
_comment_auth_rate_limit: yourphr#647 — a per-IP FIXED WINDOW on the unauthenticated sign-in routes (/api/auth/signin and /api/auth/demo-signin). Separate from the throttle above, which counts FAILURES per account and per IP: this one counts REQUESTS, because demo sign-in runs a bcrypt verify for an anonymous caller who posts nothing, and a caller who never fails is not slowed by a failure counter. Setting max-requests to 0 or less turns it OFF, deliberately — an automated suite driving real logins from one address is the case that needs that switch. A non-positive window is a typo rather than an instruction, so it falls back to 60 seconds instead of reading as 'disable the backstop'. Counters are per PROCESS, so N replicas allow N times the budget.
_comment_demo: yourphr#643 — a PUBLIC DEMO signs every visitor into one shared account with POST /api/auth/demo-signin, which posts no credentials. `enabled` is published to callers with no login (the sign-in page decides whether to offer the button); the USERNAME is never published, and the password is verified server-side and never reaches a browser. The password is GENERATED at startup and written here as an override — nobody chooses it and nobody types it — and is regenerated whenever the stored hash and this value drift apart, which is what a freshly restored seed looks like. Leaving `enabled` false, the shipped default, makes every part of this inert.
_comment_demo_reset: yourphr#645 — the ONE setting in this product that deliberately destroys a live database. It is armed three ways: demo.enabled, demo.reset-on-restart, and a baseline.dir that actually holds one (no baseline, nothing to restore, nothing destroyed). Then it still has to PROVE the database belongs to a demo: every account in it must be the demo account, the demo admin, or the bootstrap admin, or the reset is refused and the instance starts normally WITH ITS DATA INTACT. An encrypted database is refused outright — the baseline ships in a public image, so it is plaintext. Sessions need no special handling: the session key is generated at every boot, so a restart already ends every session and a returning visitor gets the sign-in page.
_comment_demo_admin: yourphr#644 — the SECOND one-click entrance: a read-only admin tour, so a reviewer can see the operator screens (Database, Logs) without an operator handing out a real admin credential. Configuration is NOT part of the tour: viewing it needs admin-system (yourphr#751), because it is how the instance defends itself and a public tour would publish the sign-in throttle. Requires demo.admin.enabled ON TOP of demo.enabled, because an admin account a stranger can enter is not something one flag should be able to open. Same credential story as the demo account: the password is generated at startup, kept here, and verified server-side — the entrance posts nothing. The account holds the demo-admin ROLE, and every write is refused for it at the door regardless of what the UI renders.
_comment_sync_budget: yourphr#759 — max-pages is what ONE resource type may fetch; max-pages-per-sync is what one source's whole sync may fetch, so a provider with years of one type cannot spend the run on it and leave the rest of the record unfetched. Go used 250 per type and 5000 overall; a type that hits either cap keeps what it fetched and SAYS it was truncated, because a partial import that looks complete is the failure worth avoiding.
_comment_upload: yourphr#736 — the largest file the Sources page's upload accepts, in bytes. A whole-record FHIR export from a large portal runs to tens of megabytes; the cap exists so a mistaken upload (a video, a disk image) is refused at the door rather than read into memory.
_comment_cda_converter: yourphr#735 — C-CDA (XML) import converts the document to FHIR through the fhir-converter service (ghcr.io/jwilleke/yourphr-cda-converter), which must run BESIDE this instance and stay internal: it receives whole medical records, so give it no published port or ingress. url is its address as this instance reaches it, e.g. http://yourphr-cda-converter:8080 — one of the named internal origins this instance may call past the SSRF guard (src/http/internal-service.ts); the other is an operator-set relay, yourphr.relay.url (yourphr#749). Ordinary settings, not environment variables (yourphr#472); read on every upload, so no restart after changing them. enabled defaults ON so that setting url is the only step; turning it off makes the Sources page say so instead of offering a conversion. Replaces Go's cda_converter.* and YOURPHR_CDA_CONVERTER_*, which this stack does not read.
_comment_authorization: yourphr#623 — permissions and roles are DATA, read from the merged configuration at startup. The permission NAMES are the enforcement contract: a role may only name one this build defines, and an unknown name refuses the boot. roles.definitions is an object, so it deep-merges PER ROLE — an operator adds a role in app-custom-config.json without restating the others. A role's permissions[] is a plain list and is replaced wholesale on override, which is intended: it is one role's list, not the catalogue. issystem marks a role this build defines; it is not the operator's to redefine out of existence, because accounts store the role name.

admin-read.description: See the operator screens — configuration, database, logs, metrics, the provider catalog

admin-system.description: Change what this instance is — configuration values, instance identity, backups, the provider catalog

user-read.description: See the list of accounts and how many the instance holds

admin.description: Runs this instance: every operator screen, and the account list.

demo-admin.description: The public demo's admin tour (yourphr#644): every operator SCREEN and none of the writing. admin-read alone, deliberately — user-read is withheld because a stranger has no business reading the account list of an instance whose front door has no lock, and admin-system is what read-only means. Read-only is NOT enforced by this list alone: the routes answer curl whatever the UI renders, so the server refuses every write for this role by default (see the demo-admin guard).

user.description: Owns their own records. The empty list is not an oversight: a member reaches their own records by OWNERSHIP, not by a permission.

anonymous.description: A role with an empty list rather than an `if` at the edge, so the unauthenticated path goes through the same evaluator as every other.

_comment_public: Keys served by GET /api/instance/public to callers with NO login (yourphr#457). Direction matters: this is an ALLOW-LIST, so a key added anywhere else in this file is private until it is named here. A deny-list would publish anything nobody remembered to list. An instance may widen it in <data>/config/app-custom-config.json.
_comment_config_secret_keys: Keys masked on the Admin Configuration screen until an admin explicitly reveals one (yourphr#458). Deliberately SHORT: masking everything outside `public` makes an operator click through the listen port and the log level, and trains them to reveal reflexively. This list is the OPPOSITE shape to `public` and that is intentional — `public` is an allow-list because a mistake exposes a value to the internet; `secret` is a DENY-LIST because a mistake shows a value to an already-authenticated admin on their own screen. A value that is an ${VAR} environment reference masks itself and needs no entry here (yourphr#622).
_comment_config_env_keys: yourphr#635 — keys OWNED BY THE ENVIRONMENT, and the variable that supplies each. A key is owned by exactly one layer, never both: these are the environment's, so they are always read-only on Admin -> Configuration (409 on write) whether or not the variable is currently set, shown with the variable's name. Making ownership conditional on the variable being set would hand the screen the source of truth whenever it is absent, which is the ambiguity this removes. The value shipped below for such a key is a BOOT FALLBACK so a fresh install comes up, not a setting. To change one: set the variable in .env and restart. Nothing here writes .env, by design.
